channel.title: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome" - causes the person to conspire against themselves

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
item.content:encoded:
Oh, I didn't know this SCP before, thanks for pointing it out to me. It is a nice one and has a similar basic concept to mine indeed.
My concept still needs some fleshing out but the core idea I want to work with is that of a physically noticeable immune reaponse to the memetic agents, not only a psychological one. Kind of like a "memetic scar tissue". I will think of ways to make it more well defined and unique. Thanks a lot for the critique!

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
item.content:encoded: I like the concept, this is a good first attempt since a lot of the site's most interesting works come from adding paranormal twists to everyday concepts, like Mount Everest being 45% corpses. Even reminds me of 1432 a little. However, I feel that more needs to be done to differentiate it from real-world variants of Delusional misidentification syndrome because in its current state it just feels like a typical mental illness resulting from seeing things man wasn't meant to (or in other words, a Tuesday for the Foundation).

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
item.content:encoded:
Those are good questions, thanks for asking them.
Real life autoimmune disease are still kinda mysterious and the specific conditions to develop them can vary a lot but two factors that seem to be important are genetics and stress. I don't think one specific SCP could cause it as the disease itself is the focus of the article and not the SCP causing ir. I am leaning towards "repetitive exposure coupled with genetics result in the syndrome".

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
item.content:encoded:
This seems like it would fit in well with the antimemetics storyline. They seem to be popular right now. I'm a big fan of it being an auto immune response that somehow manifested in a person after working with too many memetic scps.

1 question I have though is HOW did it manifest? It seems like if it was going to alter someone's regular immune response there would need to be a trigger to make it anomalous. Is another scp causing this change in the immune response from normal to anomalous? Did the researcher do something to trigger it? Was there one specific memetic scp that made the change? Would love to hear more about it.

item.title: Seeking greenlight: Anomalous Impostor Syndrome
item.content:encoded:
An anomalous version of Impostor Syndrome that causes the person to conspire against themselves.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Personal horror

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous variation of Impostor Syndrome in which the affected person believes they are an actual impostor, stealing their own memories and identity. Severe cases might end up in the subject trying to kill themselves in an attempt at returning things to their right way.

Central Narrative: An up-and-coming Foundation researcher starts to conspire against themself, to the point of hiring a hitman to kill themself. This catches the attention of the psychiatric department and an investigation begins.
After several therapy sessions the affected researcher is put through a brain scan and the anomaly is found: it is an auto immune response to the constant contact the reaearcher had had with memetic and antimemetic material. It caused their brain to stop recognizing their own memories.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
· An anomalous twist to an everyday problem, the Impostor Syndrome, a condition that causes a person to question their skills and value
· The concept of a memetic disease and a memetic immune system and how these interact with other memetic SCP articles and tales
· Potential long term characters and concepts to be used and explored by other articles and authors

Additional Notes: I haven't started writing it yet, this is the very first concept of my very first SCP article so I am open to all critics and suggestions :)
